metadata.case_name: TANG WAI TAK v. CHIU HING CONSTRUCTION & TRANSPORTATION CO LTD AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: Flexion and extension injury of neck / sprain (whiplash)
source: The above named was attended by Dr Lai Chung-Chuen at 15:55 hours on 30 July 2003 at the Accident & Emergency Department of Queen Elizabeth Hospital. He sustained neck injury whilst on duty on 30 July 2003. He sustained flexion and extension injury of neck.
The clinical diagnosis was sprain back.
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain, stiffness or tenderness only

injuries.description: Minimally bulging disc at C3/4, C4/5 and C5/6 without nerve root or cord compression
source: MRI scan of the cervical spine performed on him on 3 November 2004 revealed a minimally bulging disc at C3/4, C4/5 and C5/6 without nerve root or cord compression.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the neck

manifestations.description: tenderness (pain) at right paraspinal muscle of neck (on examination at A&E)
on and off neck pain especially at night which is aggravated by neck movement requiring relief by analgesic taken once a day
on and off dizziness especially in the morning brought on by neck rotation or concentrating at a task
reduced concentration span when driving; decreased efficiency and capacity for prolonged driving

treatments_received: attended A&E Department of Queen Elizabeth Hospital; discharged with analgesic
sick leave recommended (30 July 2003 to 2 August 2003 inclusive)
follow-up treatment at Robert Black Health Centre for about two months
referred to Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology of Caritas Medical Centre and Our Lady of Maryknoll Hospital
physiotherapy from Kowloon Hospital for two months
referral to Medical Department and ENT Department of Caritas (no abnormality detected)
MRI scan of cervical spine on 2004-11-03
treatments_future: continuous treatment on an "as and when required" basis (Dr Wong recommendation)
rest and stretching exercises during work; possible change to moderate work (Dr Wong suggestions)

losses.description: On and off neck pain and dizziness (residual symptoms) affecting concentration and driving capacity, as described: "on and off neck pain especially at night which is aggravated by neck movement requiring relief by analgesic taken once a day"; "on and off dizziness especially in the morning brought on by neck rotation or concentrating at a task."
